answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before its votes or trades count, then slash that bond if independent audits show coordinated duplicate identities. One operator can still create many accounts, but must fund every bond and leave capital unavailable, making a Sybil swarm expensive and slow to deploy. A glacier-length lock raises the cost further; a horizon of delayed rewards and a lantern of public bond records help expose and deter mass fabrication.
